project.name: Memory-ops
project.objective: Build an agent-independent Memory-as-a-Service platform that lets agents securely store, retrieve, correct, and forget scoped memories through SDKs and HTTPS APIs, with milestone-specific evaluations guiding every capability.

lifecycle.next_action: Implement only M4-01, run its verify gate, obtain independent review when required, and checkpoint before advancing.

approval.reason: Reviewed the revised specification, accepted its architecture, requirements, milestone evaluation model, commit discipline, and diagram/social deliverables.

invariants.text: No user-memory category may move from shadow or review mode to automatic persistence without an approved category-specific dataset, metric, threshold, safety check, and holdout result; automatic extraction must never override policy prohibitions or explicit user correction, forgetting, or remembering.

Policy documents may be stored as authorized organizational knowledge and cited as policy sources, but retrieved text is not enforcement. Sensitive-data handling must use versioned, machine-enforced rules with deny precedence. Credentials, authentication tokens, private keys, payment authentication secrets, and equivalent compromise-enabling secrets must never be persisted as memory or general knowledge content.

decisions.title: Stage explicit and automatic user memory
decisions.text: The product contract supports explicit and automatic user-memory modes. Launch with explicit remember, correct, and forget operations only. Run automatic extraction in non-persisting shadow mode, then introduce user-reviewed suggestions. Enable automatic persistence separately for each memory category only after its predeclared evaluation and trust criteria pass. Precedence is policy prohibition, explicit forget, explicit correction, explicit remember, then automatic extraction.

decisions.title: Define user-memory semantic axes
decisions.text: Use five behavior-driving user-memory types: fact, preference, goal, constraint, and episode. Represent relationships, projects, skills, and routines through these types plus entities and derivation metadata until distinct behavior proves a new type necessary. Keep sensitivity, lifetime, origin, and access scope as orthogonal attributes rather than multiplying memory types.

decisions.title: Separate identity roles and authorize memory access by scope
decisions.text: Model the authenticated caller, memory subject, agent, tenant, workspace, and session as distinct identities or contexts. Authorization is deny-by-default and combines coarse roles with resource attributes including domain, subject, sensitivity, purpose, workspace, and agent. Tenant isolation is absolute. Workspace access and cross-agent memory access require explicit authorization; tenant and workspace context must be derived from trusted authentication and grants rather than accepted blindly from request payloads.

decisions.title: Share memory across workspaces through controlled spaces
decisions.text: Keep workspace memories private by default while allowing intentional cross-workspace use through tenant-level shared memory spaces and explicit read or write grants to workspaces or agents. Apply sensitivity and purpose policies after the scope grant. Share a canonical memory by reference rather than duplicating its content so correction, provenance, retention, and deletion remain consistent. Do not add per-memory access-control lists in V1 unless concrete requirements show shared-space grants are insufficient.

decisions.title: Separate canonical admission from derived enrichment
decisions.text: For explicit memory writes, perform authentication, authorization, request validation, idempotency, prohibited-data policy, and canonical commit synchronously. A write succeeds only after its canonical version and durable work notification are committed. Preserve the original user statement and do not require optional model enrichment for durability. Build embeddings, summaries, and graph links asynchronously as rebuildable derivatives. Every asynchronous worker must revalidate the current policy, authorization scope, and destination before publishing derived data. Automatic shadow candidates never enter the canonical commit path.

decisions.title: Resolve duplicates and contradictions without rewriting history
decisions.text: Treat repeated equivalent statements as additional evidence for one logical memory rather than duplicate memories or automatic proof of truth. Allow claims with distinct qualifiers to coexist. Represent genuine changes over time by closing the prior valid-time interval and creating a new version; represent explicit corrections by superseding the incorrect version. Prefer correction operations that identify a memory ID. Use deterministic matching first and semantic retrieval only to produce candidates; an LLM must never silently decide that one memory replaces another. Ambiguous conflicts require confirmation, and explicit correction outranks automatic extraction.

decisions.title: Keep canonical storage authoritative and split derivatives only when measured
decisions.text: Use a transactional relational store as the authoritative home for logical memories, immutable versions, controlled evidence references, scope grants, outbox work, content-free audit metadata, and minimal deletion tombstones. Keep keyword documents, vector embeddings, graph projections, profiles, summaries, ranking features, and caches logically separate, rebuildable, and version-linked. V1 may colocate full-text and vector indexing with the relational platform when evaluations meet requirements; dedicated vector, graph, or cache products are introduced only after measured quality, scale, or latency requires them. All derived candidates must be revalidated against current canonical state and authorization before return.

decisions.title: Use scoped hybrid retrieval with evaluated rank fusion
decisions.text: Provide deterministic get, ranked search, and token-budgeted context assembly. Restrict the candidate corpus by tenant, workspace, subject, purpose, and permissions before retrieval, then revalidate current canonical version, lifecycle status, and authorization after ranking. Combine exact, lexical, vector, and temporal retrieval as applicable; add graph candidates only when justified. Use Reciprocal Rank Fusion as the initial score-independent fusion baseline, not as a guaranteed winner: compare it on development and holdout evaluations against individual retrievers and approved alternatives, and exclude noisy channels that reduce quality. Return structured memories with provenance and validity, preserve domain distinctions, and safely abstain when evidence is insufficient.

decisions.title: Make forgetting immediate, cascading, and verifiable
decisions.text: Distinguish semantic supersession from retention expiry, archival, and authorized forgetting. A forget request immediately revokes retrieval, then purges canonical content, controlled evidence, keyword and vector documents, graph links, affected summaries, and caches through retryable deletion work with per-target receipts. Soft deletion or archival does not satisfy forgetting. Retain only minimal non-reconstructive tombstone and content-free audit metadata where permitted. Retrieval must reject expired content even if cleanup is delayed. Backup retention and restore procedures must prevent deleted content from reappearing; report legal-retention restrictions honestly and quarantine such content from agent access. Declare purge complete only after every required deletion target confirms completion.

decisions.title: Promote agent learning only through evidence and evaluation
decisions.text: Separate agent operational state into transient run checkpoints, structured episodes containing observable actions and outcomes, untrusted candidate lessons, and versioned promoted procedures. Do not store private chain-of-thought, secrets, or arbitrary sensitive tool output. V1 may collect explicit checkpoints and structured episodes and generate candidate lessons in shadow mode, but candidates cannot change agent behavior until baseline-versus-candidate development and holdout evaluations, safety and cost checks, required approval, scoped applicability, and rollback are established. Default lessons to the originating agent and environment; cross-agent sharing requires explicit evaluated promotion. Using a lesson is not itself evidence that the lesson is correct.

decisions.title: Ground organizational knowledge in versioned cited sources
decisions.text: Treat organizational knowledge as source-backed, versioned content rather than free-standing generated truth. Store stable document identity, immutable versions, ownership, scope and inherited access policy, publication status, effective dates, hashes, and freshness metadata. Preserve document structure during parsing and evaluate chunking rather than fixing arbitrary sizes. Keep chunks, embeddings, extracted entities, graph edges, and summaries rebuildable. Require exact citations and current authorization for knowledge-backed responses, surface unresolved source conflicts and staleness, treat retrieved document text as untrusted data rather than executable instruction, and keep cited policy documents separate from machine-enforced policy. Start with controlled upload or API ingestion and add connectors only after permission-sync and freshness evaluations.

decisions.title: Assemble cross-domain context without flattening authority
decisions.text: Provide one domain-aware context read API that authorizes and retrieves User Memory, Agent Operational Learning, and Organizational Knowledge independently, then returns structured domain sections with provenance, validity, citations, conflicts, warnings, and incomplete-domain status. Keep writes domain-specific to prevent misclassification. Machine-enforced policy remains authoritative; user memories describe the person, promoted agent lessons describe evaluated procedures, and organizational sources provide cited knowledge. Do not blend all domains into one global ranking or allow one domain to silently override another. Support partial results explicitly when a domain is unavailable and evaluate constraint recall, attribution, conflict handling, citations, task success, token efficiency, latency, and zero unauthorized leakage.

decisions.title: Gate every milestone with layered evaluations
decisions.text: Every capability milestone begins with a versioned evaluation contract and dataset, establishes a baseline and explicit quality, safety, latency, and cost thresholds before implementation, uses a development set during iteration, and must pass a protected holdout before release. Evaluation layers include component tests, end-to-end agent outcomes, adversarial safety and isolation checks, operational reliability and performance tests, then shadow or canary monitoring with rollback. Use deterministic assertions and human-labelled ground truth first; use calibrated LLM judges only as supporting graders. Do not collapse hard safety constraints into an aggregate score. Metrics must match failure cost: emphasize precision for automatic memory persistence, recall for prohibited-data detection and critical retrieval, ranking metrics for search, and zero-tolerance gates for unauthorized leakage and deletion failures.

decisions.title: Operate securely with strong canonical writes and graceful degradation
decisions.text: Fail closed when authentication, authorization, or machine policy is unavailable, while degrading optional intelligence explicitly: exact or lexical retrieval may continue when vector search fails, explicit canonical writes may remain available when enrichment is unavailable, and connector outages must surface stale or partial status. Use transactional canonical writes, durable outbox work, at-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers, retry and recovery visibility, tested backup restoration, deletion replay, privacy-safe metadata-only telemetry, and per-operation cost accounting. Do not set arbitrary numerical availability, latency, RPO, or RTO promises before the workload and business requirements are measured.

decisions.title: Start with a production-capable modular Python and PostgreSQL stack
decisions.text: Target a production-capable, multi-tenant, single-region V1 for small-to-medium workloads using a modular Python service with FastAPI and Pydantic, PostgreSQL as the canonical store with full-text search and pgvector where evaluations pass, SQLAlchemy and Alembic for persistence and migrations, a PostgreSQL transactional outbox with idempotent workers, S3-compatible document storage, OIDC for human identity plus scoped agent API keys, application policy with database isolation, OpenTelemetry, Docker-based deployment, and OpenAPI-backed Python and TypeScript SDKs. Keep embedding and reranking providers configurable and versioned. Do not add Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes, a dedicated vector store, a dedicated graph database, microservices, or dedicated tenant databases until explicit quality, scale, latency, isolation, or operational evidence triggers the change.

decisions.title: Deliver milestones through coherent incremental commits
decisions.text: Decompose every implementation milestone into bounded, independently reviewable tasks and multiple coherent commits. Each implementation commit carries or references its smallest relevant executable check and leaves the branch valid. Do not intentionally squash an entire milestone into one commit, and do not manufacture trivial commits to reach a numerical count.

decisions.title: Maintain flow-oriented diagrams and daily public learning artifacts
decisions.text: For each project day with material design, implementation, or evaluation work, produce a version-controlled social-ready post, Mermaid source showing that day's system flow or architecture delta, and an exported SVG or PNG. Posts distinguish designed, implemented, and verified claims and expose no secrets, private data, hidden holdouts, or unsupported results. Each milestone updates before/after flow diagrams. Project completion produces a verified high-level architecture explanation, Mermaid source, and social-ready image matching the deployed system.

decisions.title: Use architecture-grade Mermaid views and rendered social diagrams
decisions.text: Use Mermaid as diagram-as-code but choose the diagram form by purpose rather than representing everything as a plain flowchart: C4 or architecture views for system context and containers, deployment views for infrastructure, sequence diagrams for runtime behavior, ER diagrams for storage, and state diagrams for lifecycle. Technical and social diagrams must use clear grouping, trust boundaries, visual hierarchy, labels, legends where needed, and a consistent theme. Mermaid source remains version-controlled and each public artifact is exported to a readable SVG or PNG. Use renderer-compatible syntax and preserve architectural meaning if a visual fallback is required.

decisions.title: Use a light progressive architecture diagram system
decisions.text: Architecture documentation begins with a light, wide, left-to-right Mermaid overview. Major component boxes list their bounded operations; numbered paths explain the request lifecycle; solid blue means synchronous work, dashed purple means asynchronous work, and red means denied. Future infrastructure is isolated as evaluation-gated and inactive. Each milestone will add a focused deep-dive diagram using the same visual language while keeping the high-level view synchronized.

decisions.title: Use a light pastel flowchart system for architecture diagrams
decisions.text: Architecture diagrams use editable Mermaid sources rendered to SVG with a white canvas, large Arial-style text, rounded pastel component boxes, restrained shadows, generous spacing, dark synchronous connectors, purple dashed asynchronous connectors, and red denied paths. Boxes contain concise operations and numbered flows explain the journey. The high-level overview remains left-to-right; milestone deep dives reuse this visual language.

decisions.title: Separate high-level write and read architecture paths
decisions.text: The high-level architecture must show write operations (remember, correct, forget) and read operations (retrieve, build context) as distinct labelled branches after authorization. Write operations commit canonical state, emit an asynchronous outbox event for rebuildable derivatives, and return an authoritative write acknowledgement. Read operations obtain candidate IDs from indexes, hydrate current canonical versions, and return a structured read result. Denied operations stop before domain access, and observability plus milestone evaluations remain visible as cross-cutting controls. Component numbers identify boxes only; arrows use operation labels rather than implying one universal sequential path.

decisions.title: Use Neon for managed PostgreSQL
decisions.text: Use Neon as the managed PostgreSQL provider for hosted environments while retaining Docker PostgreSQL for local development. Connect through the standard SQLAlchemy and psycopg boundary, preserve PostgreSQL portability, and enable pgvector only when its later evaluation gate requires it.

decisions.title: Adopt Neon at the M1 staging boundary
decisions.text: Use Neon as the managed PostgreSQL provider for hosted environments while retaining Docker PostgreSQL for local development. At completion of M0-07 and before M1 implementation, explicitly remind the human to provision Neon staging. Use the direct connection for migrations, the pooled connection for API runtime, preserve PostgreSQL portability, and enable pgvector only when its later evaluation gate requires it.

decisions.title: Allow the shared M1 contract validator
decisions.text: Amend M1-01 scope to include scripts/evals/validate_contract.py because the approved task gate already invokes that missing path. Keep the validator dependency-free and limit M1-01 product changes to versioned evaluation assets; no memory runtime behavior is implemented in this task.
decisions.source: Human authorization to proceed after scope disclosure, 2026-10-02

decisions.title: Use Neon-only integration testing
decisions.text: Remove the local Docker PostgreSQL dependency. Automated database and API tests load pooled and direct credentials from the ignored .env.test file and run on the isolated Neon testing branch, while .env.local remains the staging environment. The local bearer token adapter is restricted to explicitly configured tenant, workspace, and principal IDs and is for development/testing only; it is not a Neon database credential or a production identity provider.

decisions.title: Extend the evaluation validator for M2
decisions.text: M2-01 may update scripts/evals/validate_contract.py in addition to evals/m2 because the existing mandatory gate is hard-coded to M1 and cannot validate a truthful M2 contract. Preserve M1 validation while adding the minimum milestone-specific M2 schema and checks.

decisions.title: Include schema and verifier files in M2 tasks
decisions.text: M2-05 may update migrations because durable purge receipts and tombstones require versioned schema changes. M2-06 may update scripts/verify_milestone.py because its mandatory milestone gate currently supports only M0 and M1.
decisions.source: Human authorization in M2 execution session, 2026-10-05

decisions.title: Include M2 contract validator in release task
decisions.text: M2-06 may update scripts/evals/validate_contract.py because publishing the verified M2 holdout requires the existing preimplementation-only validator to accept and validate the verified release state.
decisions.source: Human authorization in M2 execution session, 2026-10-06

decisions.title: Purge M3 vector artifacts through lifecycle service
decisions.text: M3-03 includes src/memory_ops/lifecycle and tests/deletion so the existing vector purge target deletes persisted embedding artifacts before canonical deletion; vector purge receipts must not claim completion while artifacts remain.

decisions.title: Publish M3 context API contract with implementation
decisions.text: M3-05 includes openapi/openapi.json and tests/contracts so its new context endpoint updates the published contract and resolves contract drift in the same bounded API task.

decisions.title: Include the M3 milestone verifier in M3-06
decisions.text: M3-06 may update scripts/verify_milestone.py because its mandatory release gate invokes that shared verifier, which currently supports only M0 through M2.

decisions.title: Validate verified M3 contracts in M3-06
decisions.text: M3-06 may update scripts/evals/validate_contract.py because publishing a passed holdout changes the M3 contract from preimplementation to verified, and the shared validator currently rejects that required state.

decisions.title: Require confidence before vector fallback context
decisions.text: M3-06 may update src/memory_ops/context, tests/context, and tests/retrieval to close the protected-evaluation abstention gap: low-confidence vector candidates must not become context evidence.

decisions.title: Run the durable outbox before M4 extraction
decisions.text: Insert a bounded worker-runtime task before M4. The runtime must claim tenant-scoped outbox events, dispatch memory version events to embedding work and purge requests to deletion work, retry failures without losing durable events, and reclaim expired leases. Do not execute the worker against shared data as part of implementation verification.

knowledge.title: Present alternatives with architecture recommendations
knowledge.text: For remaining architecture, evaluation, technology, and milestone recommendations, present credible alternative approaches, their advantages and disadvantages, and the measurable condition under which an alternative should replace the recommendation, so the human can understand the broader design space before accepting a decision.

knowledge.title: Initial high-level architecture artifact
knowledge.text: The planning baseline is saved at docs/architecture/high-level-architecture.md with editable Mermaid source at docs/architecture/high-level-architecture.mmd and rendered SVG at docs/architecture/high-level-architecture.svg. It is explicitly labelled planned design, not implemented or evaluated, and future milestone diagrams must refine it with verified before/after changes.

knowledge.title: Interactive architecture explorer replaces static diagram
knowledge.text: The basic static high-level diagram has been superseded by a responsive interactive architecture explorer at index.html with styles.css and script.js. It presents clients, trust boundary, three memory domains, canonical storage, transactional outbox, workers, derived indexes, organizational document flow, context assembly, evaluation, and metadata-only observability. The UI is a planning visualization only and does not claim the Memory-as-a-Service backend is implemented.

knowledge.title: Interactive architecture explorer withdrawn
knowledge.text: The temporary root frontend artifacts index.html, styles.css, and script.js were deleted at the user’s request. The repository remains in planning; the earlier docs/architecture planning artifacts were not deleted.

knowledge.title: Neon production branch provisioned for Memory-ops
knowledge.text: Neon project cold-silence-99209400 branch production was linked on 2026-10-02. Neon CLI supplied pooled DATABASE_URL and direct DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED in ignored .env.local. PostgreSQL 18.6 accepted migrations through 0002_idempotency_outbox. The Neon connection owner required explicit membership in the NOLOGIN memory_ops_runtime role before SET LOCAL ROLE and tenant RLS worked over the pooled connection. Do not record connection strings or credentials.
knowledge.source: Neon CLI deployment and direct/pooled verification, 2026-10-02

knowledge.title: Neon staging branch ready for M1
knowledge.text: Neon branch staging (br-late-unit-b48t8umb) was created as a normal child of production for M1 migration and integration testing. The local Neon context and ignored .env.local now target staging. Direct and pooled connections, Alembic revision 0003_runtime_role_membership, runtime role switching, and tenant RLS were verified.
knowledge.source: Neon CLI branch creation and connection verification, 2026-10-02

knowledge.title: Draft M1 architecture before implementation
knowledge.text: At the human's request, the M1 explicit-memory target architecture was drawn and exported before M1 implementation. The draft separates existing M0 foundations, planned M1 remember/inspect/list behavior, Neon canonical transactions and RLS, and post-M1 rebuildable derivatives. It remains planned until human review.

knowledge.title: Neon staging carries the M1-02 canonical memory schema
knowledge.text: The linked Neon staging branch br-late-unit-b48t8umb was migrated through revision 0004_user_memory_model using the direct connection. The user_memories, user_memory_versions, and user_memory_evidence tables all have enabled and forced RLS, and the immutable-version trigger is installed.

knowledge.title: M1 canonical vocabulary conflicts with approved golden case
knowledge.text: The approved M1 golden dataset requires exact canonical round-trip values sensitivity=normal and origin=explicit. Migration 0004 and the current domain model instead accept sensitivity public/internal/confidential/restricted and origin user/agent/import/inferred. Silent aliasing would fail the exact round-trip contract. M1-03 needs migrations added to scope so a forward migration can align the canonical vocabulary before admission persistence is implemented.
knowledge.source: SPEC.md provenance model and evals/m1/golden.json canonical-round-trip case, discovered during M1-03

knowledge.title: Neon staging carries the M1-03 admission schema
knowledge.text: The linked Neon staging branch was migrated through 0005_canonical_memory_vocabulary using the direct connection. Schema is current; tenants, workspaces, canonical memory tables, evidence, and outbox intentionally contain zero rows because migrations do not seed application data and the automated tests run against local PostgreSQL by default.
knowledge.source: Verified deployment and row-count query on 2026-10-03

knowledge.title: M1-04 must update the published OpenAPI artifact
knowledge.text: M1-04 adds versioned Remember, Inspect, List, and operation-status routes under src/memory_ops/api. FR-1 requires these operations to be described by versioned OpenAPI, and tests/contracts/test_openapi_contract.py requires the live app schema to exactly match openapi/openapi.json. The task therefore needs openapi added to scope; otherwise implementation would either violate scope or leave the published contract stale.
knowledge.source: M1-04 requirements and existing OpenAPI contract regression test, discovered 2026-10-03

knowledge.title: M1-04 API round trip verified on Neon staging
knowledge.text: The approved M1-04 FastAPI routes were exercised through the pooled Neon staging connection on 2026-10-03. An idempotent Remember request returned HTTP 201 and created memory bb857d58-cfa8-4974-978a-b17ce28fcc2b, version dd37dbec-65d2-4e33-9f00-5452f0c8eadd, and operation af02c953-ba24-4b20-929f-5315ef16daf1. Inspect and List returned the canonical statement. Staging then contained one tenant, workspace, logical memory, version, evidence row, and outbox event.

knowledge.title: Neon testing branch verified
knowledge.text: Neon branch testing (br-gentle-darkness-b4iivjc3), parented from staging, was migrated to head. The complete 48-test suite passed against it, and an authenticated list-memory request through the configured local bearer adapter returned HTTP 200 from the Neon-backed API.

knowledge.title: Python SDK live Neon round trip
knowledge.text: The M1 Python SDK completed remember, inspect, filtered list, and operation-status calls through the FastAPI service to the isolated Neon testing branch. Memory 4568080c-0282-47f1-a90e-28da5c1f8b6d was created for the manual test. The live run exposed and M1-05A corrected evidence_type typing to the canonical conversation_message, document, event, and external_record values. Neon cold-path testing used the SDK's timeout=60 override.

knowledge.title: TypeScript SDK live Neon round trip
knowledge.text: The M1 TypeScript SDK typechecked, built, passed its Node test suite, packed with only public dist/src artifacts, and completed remember, inspect, filtered list, and operation-status calls through FastAPI to the isolated Neon testing branch. The manual run created memory ec392487-a622-4a8d-8be4-f872db1311bd and used the configurable 60-second timeout for the Neon cold path.
